title: Code review session covering a naming decision, a security fix, and a deferred nice-to-have
notes: Long session spanning three unrelated topics in one code-review pass: a naming decision, a security fix, and a deferred nice-to-have that is explicitly deprioritized, not actioned.

turns.text: Reviewing your PR now. First thing — you named the new function getUsrPrefs(), can we spell out 'User' fully? Abbreviations like that make grepping harder later.
Fair, renaming to getUserPreferences() across the three call sites — 'Usr' isn't used consistently elsewhere in the codebase anyway, so this brings it in line with existing naming conventions.

Thanks. Bigger issue — the new /api/export endpoint doesn't check that the requesting user owns the account being exported, just that they're authenticated at all. Anyone logged in could export anyone else's data by ID.

Good catch, that's a real authorization bug (IDOR). Adding an ownership check: the endpoint now verifies req.user.id matches the accountId being exported, returning 403 if not, before any export logic runs.
Please add a regression test for that too, this class of bug is exactly what we don't want to reintroduce.
Added a test asserting a 403 when userA requests userB's export, plus the existing happy-path test for exporting your own account.
One more thought, lower priority — could the export also support a CSV format, not just JSON? Some users have asked for that.

Technically straightforward to add, but I'd defer it — it's not related to this PR's scope and there's no urgent need yet, just occasional user requests. I'll leave it as a nice-to-have for a future PR rather than scope-creeping this one.
Agreed, not now. Approve the rest once the rename and the auth fix are in.
Pushed both fixes — renamed function and the ownership check with its regression test. Ready for re-review.

gold_atoms.text: Rename getUsrPrefs() to getUserPreferences() across its call sites, to avoid non-standard abbreviations and match existing codebase naming conventions.
The /api/export endpoint only checked that the requester was authenticated, not that they owned the account being exported — an IDOR bug letting any logged-in user export any other user's data by ID.
Add an ownership check to /api/export verifying req.user.id matches the accountId being exported, returning 403 otherwise, before running any export logic.
Add a regression test asserting a 403 when userA requests userB's export, alongside the existing happy-path self-export test.
Adding CSV export format support (in addition to JSON) was raised as a user-requested nice-to-have but explicitly deferred to a future PR, out of scope for this one.
